items.claim: The row's declared divine-title signal is asserted with two byte-tier labels but no quoted Hebrew form anywhere in the row, and its closing-title framing omits the same title's third site in the chapter while the span's own bytes do name Israel.
items.evidence: The onset splice re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Isa.41.17, and both parashah claims verify against the mark inventory under the claimed type (PE at oshb:Isa.41.16, PE at oshb:Isa.41.20); no paseq and no ketiv/qere note falls inside oshb:Isa.41.17-Isa.41.20, so in-span disclosure is complete. The title claim, however, carries 'tier: byte' at oshb:Isa.41.16 and oshb:Isa.41.20 with no Hebrew run quoted for it: the forms are וּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.20, byte tier) and בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּתְהַלָּֽל (oshb:Isa.41.16, byte tier), and a title claim with no quoted form is insufficient engagement on the row's own second signal. A title sweep over chapter 41 returns three verses (sweep: 3 verses, the qadosh-Israel title, MT 41:14, 41:16, 41:20), so קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.41.14, byte tier) is a third, non-closing site one span back that the recurring-closing-title framing does not disclose. Separately, 'without renaming Israel explicitly' sits against the onset verse's own אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.17, byte tier): the name stands in both the first and the last verse of the span, in two different divine titles. The seam itself is not contested -- the PE marks and the topic onset hold.

items.claim: Disclosure-object coverage is complete and byte-correct, but two byte-true devices straddle the row's own close seam undisclosed and the cross-span summons echo is asserted with no Hebrew form.
items.evidence: Every disclosure object inside oshb:Isa.41.21-Isa.41.29 verifies and is disclosed -- PE at oshb:Isa.41.20 and oshb:Isa.41.29, paseq at oshb:Isa.41.22 (tallied, no intra-verse position asserted), ketiv/qere at oshb:Isa.41.23 -- the fullest symmetry in the cluster, and the idol addressee is byte-supported by the 'that we may know that you are gods' clause at oshb:Isa.41.23. Two byte-true devices cross the 41:29|42:1 seam without disclosure: the verse-initial particle at הֵ֣ן כֻּלָּ֔ם אָ֥וֶן (oshb:Isa.41.29, byte tier) is answered immediately by הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.1, byte tier) -- a verse-initial sweep of that particle returns 18 verses book-wide, four of them clustered at MT 41:11, 41:24, 41:29, 42:1 (sweep: 18 verses, verse-initial hen, skeleton tier) -- and ר֥וּחַ וָתֹ֖הוּ (oshb:Isa.41.29, byte tier) is answered by רוּחִי֙ עָלָ֔יו (oshb:Isa.42.1, byte tier). Both argue that the servant presentation answers the idol verdict across the cut, which the PE mark and the speaker change do not by themselves dispose of. The 41:1 echo is asserted with no quoted form; it is byte-real -- יַחְדָּ֖ו לַמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט נִקְרָֽבָה (oshb:Isa.41.1, byte tier) against קָרְב֥וּ רִֽיבְכֶ֖ם and הַגִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ עֲצֻמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם (oshb:Isa.41.21, byte tier) -- but unengaged at the byte level, so the rival architecture it discloses rests on English idiom rather than on the shared roots that actually carry it.

items.claim: The four-verse bound rests on an envelope that the bytes make a thread, and on a frame onset labelled 'tier: byte' with no frame form quoted -- the byte arm of a frame-based seam claim is missing.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier and PE at oshb:Isa.42.4 and oshb:Isa.41.29 verify against the mark inventory; no paseq or ketiv/qere note falls inside oshb:Isa.42.1-Isa.42.4. The bracket argument does not hold as stated: the justice-noun stands in three of the span's four verses (sweep: 3 verses, the mishpat noun in chapter 42, MT 42:1, 42:3, 42:4, skeleton tier) -- מִשְׁפָּ֖ט לַגּוֹיִ֥ם יוֹצִֽיא (oshb:Isa.42.1, byte tier), לֶאֱמֶ֖ת יוֹצִ֥יא מִשְׁפָּֽט (oshb:Isa.42.3, byte tier), יָשִׂ֥ים בָּאָ֖רֶץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט (oshb:Isa.42.4, byte tier) -- with the same verb repeated at the first and the medial site, so the term is a sustained thread through the unit, not an envelope closing it. The seam claim then labels 'oshb:Isa.42.5, tier: byte' with nothing quoted: the frame form is כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, byte tier), a divine frame carrying the ha-El title (the royal-messenger uses of this formula sit only in the narrative zone, not here), and naming whose frame it is while quoting it is exactly what this seam argument owes. Undisclosed across that same seam: the earth-noun runs יָשִׂ֥ים בָּאָ֖רֶץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט straight into רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ (oshb:Isa.42.5, byte tier); and the verse-initial particle answering oshb:Isa.41.29 at הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.1, byte tier) crosses the onset seam unremarked.

items.claim: The row locates a count-only paseq inside a named clause, leaves a byte-true answer pair straddling its close seam undisclosed, and labels an unquoted cross-span echo 'tier: byte' on uneven byte support.
items.evidence: Credit first: the frame is quoted in full at byte tier and its owner is correctly named -- כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, byte tier) is a divine frame with the ha-El title, and PE at oshb:Isa.42.9 and oshb:Isa.42.4 verify. Three defects. (1) The paseq at oshb:Isa.42.5 is real in the inventory, but the row places it 'inside the divine-frame clause opening this span'; that layer is count-only and intra-verse position is unsourceable, and the row's own disclaimer of a position claim does not cure the clause it has just located it in. (2) The close seam carries an undisclosed answer pair: וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ אֲנִ֣י מַגִּ֔יד (oshb:Isa.42.9, byte tier) is picked up one verse later by שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.10, byte tier), and the praise-noun the span itself withholds from idols at וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י לַפְּסִילִֽים (oshb:Isa.42.8, byte tier) is what the following verses render, at that same form and at וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ בָּאִיִּ֥ים יַגִּֽידוּ (oshb:Isa.42.12, byte tier) (sweep: 3 verses, the tehillah noun in chapter 42, MT 42:8, 42:10, 42:12; 2 verses, the kavod noun, MT 42:8, 42:12, skeleton tier). That argues continuity against the cut and is owed a disclosure. (3) The backward echo is labelled 'oshb:Isa.41.22, oshb:Isa.41.26, tier: byte' with no form quoted, and the byte support is uneven: the former-things noun is shared with oshb:Isa.41.22, whereas oshb:Isa.41.26 carries only the root in its from-the-beginning adverbial -- one tier label covering two unlike objects.

items.claim: Every cited mark and the onset form verify, but a high-confidence cut leaves a byte-true catchword pair straddling its onset seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: The onset splice re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Isa.42.10 and the plural-imperative form-class claim stands on the pointed bytes and on both witnesses' renderings; PE at oshb:Isa.42.9 and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.42.13 both verify against the mark inventory under the claimed type, never conflated, and no paseq or ketiv/qere note falls inside oshb:Isa.42.10-Isa.42.13, so in-span disclosure is complete. The gap is cross-seam: the new-song phrase שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.10, byte tier) takes up the new-things declaration one verse back at וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ אֲנִ֣י מַגִּ֔יד (oshb:Isa.42.9, byte tier), and the praise-noun and glory-noun both run from oshb:Isa.42.8 into this span at וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ בָּאִיִּ֥ים יַגִּֽידוּ (oshb:Isa.42.12, byte tier) (sweep: 3 verses, the tehillah noun in chapter 42, MT 42:8, 42:10, 42:12; 2 verses, the kavod noun, MT 42:8, 42:12, skeleton tier). A device that byte-true across the row's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed, and this row declares high confidence with no cross-seam disclosure at all. The cut itself is not overturned -- the form shift from first-person divine speech to plural imperative is byte-plain and the mark corroborates it -- but the confidence band is carrying an undisclosed rival.

items.claim: Both bounds, both parashah claims, and the one seam-adjacent cross-seam device all verify in the bytes, and the row discloses that device instead of absorbing it.
items.evidence: The onset splice re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Isa.42.14, and the first-person self-declaration form-class claim stands on the pointed bytes (the sequence of 1cs forms opening the verse) and on both witnesses' renderings. SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.42.13 and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.42.17 both verify against the mark inventory under the claimed type, with PE never conflated with SAMEKH, and no paseq and no ketiv/qere note falls inside oshb:Isa.42.14-Isa.42.17, so span-relevant disclosure symmetry is satisfied without remainder. A stem-level check of both of this row's seams returns exactly one straddling item, the blindness lexeme running from וְהוֹלַכְתִּ֣י עִוְרִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.42.16, byte tier) into oshb:Isa.42.18-Isa.42.19 (sweep: 5 verses, the blind lexeme in chapters 42-43, MT 42:7, 42:16, 42:18, 42:19, 43:8, skeleton tier) -- and the row discloses precisely that as a cross-seam echo rather than merging the spans. The close is byte-consistent too: the idol-trusters of oshb:Isa.42.17 are third-person plural forms, grammatically distinct from the plural imperatives opening oshb:Isa.42.18, so the rejected rival is refused on the bytes and not on rendering.

items.claim: The row's unnamed-referent prose is silent about its own span naming Jacob and Israel, and both of its seams carry byte-true devices it does not disclose.
items.evidence: Disclosure objects are complete and correct -- SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.42.17, PE at oshb:Isa.42.25, and both ketiv/qere notes at oshb:Isa.42.20 and oshb:Isa.42.24 verify against the inventories -- and the internal hearing-root chain (sweep: 4 verses, the shama root in MT 42:18, 42:20, 42:23, 42:24, skeleton tier) genuinely supports holding the eight verses as one unit against the 42:21 cut the row tests. The referent is rightly left open; the defect is what is left unsaid. The row states the figure is designated 'without further identifying the referent', while the span's own bytes name the plundered party at יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.24, byte tier) -- the strongest in-span datum bearing on the held question, and undisclosed even though the row cites that verse for its ketiv/qere note. Both seams also carry undisclosed byte-true devices: the blindness lexeme reaches into this span's opening from oshb:Isa.42.16 (sweep: 5 verses, the blind lexeme in chapters 42-43, MT 42:7, 42:16, 42:18, 42:19, 43:8, skeleton tier), and across the close seam וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.25, byte tier) is answered directly by וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר בָּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.43.2, byte tier) while the two names recur at בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier).

items.claim: The onset argument rests on an adversative and a divine frame the row never quotes, its close seam is argued against a byte-mislabelled rival, and the seam it cuts carries an undisclosed answer pair.
items.evidence: Both splices re-collate at byte tier and no mark, paseq, or ketiv/qere note falls inside oshb:Isa.43.1-Isa.43.7, so nothing in-span is owed. But the row argues 'the adversative onset' and a divine address while splicing only the participial epithets that follow it: the frame is וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier), one of only two divine-speech frames in this cluster's whole span (sweep: 2 verses, the koh-amar formula within Isa 41:17-43:7, MT 42:5 and 43:1, both divine-owned, neither royal-messenger, skeleton tier) -- a frame-based seam claim owes the frame form. The rival is byte-mislabelled: the gathered-nations address is כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, byte tier), whereas oshb:Isa.43.8 reads הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (byte tier), a summons of the blind people that ties back to oshb:Isa.42.18-Isa.42.19, so the rival as described begins one verse later than the row places it. Across the onset seam, וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ (oshb:Isa.42.25, byte tier) is answered directly by וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר בָּֽךְ (oshb:Isa.43.2, byte tier) and the name pair of oshb:Isa.42.24 recurs at בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier) -- undisclosed. Finally the parashah citation is keyed with a web: prefix on an MT-keyed single-witness layer; the coordinate is identity-numbered so the arithmetic holds, but the witness keying is wrong for that layer.
